Short-Term Effect on Dog: Supports vision, immune system, skin health
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Toxicity (hypervitaminosis A): bone pain, calcification of soft tissues, liver damage. Accumulates in fat.
Notes for App: Fat-soluble — accumulates. Flag if product has BOTH liver as ingredient AND synthetic Vitamin A added.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Supports nerve function, energy metabolism
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Deficiency is more dangerous than excess. Excess excreted in urine. Very low toxicity risk.
Notes for App: Safe synthetic. Deficiency causes neurological issues. Flag if absent in adult formula.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Energy production, healthy skin and eyes
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Minimal toxicity risk. Excess safely excreted. Urine may turn yellow (harmless).
Notes for App: Very safe. Synthetic form identical to natural.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: DNA repair, metabolism, skin health
Long-Term Risk (Excess): High doses: liver damage, flushing, GI issues. Dogs are sensitive to niacin deficiency (black tongue disease).
Notes for App: Deficiency causes pellagra-like symptoms in dogs. Flag absence in budget foods.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Hormone synthesis, energy metabolism
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Very low toxicity. Excess excreted. GI upset only at extreme doses.
Notes for App: Safe synthetic form. Rarely causes issues.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Protein metabolism, neurotransmitter production, immune function
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Long-term excess: peripheral neuropathy (nerve damage in limbs), loss of coordination, sensory dysfunction.
Notes for App: Safe at normal levels but toxic in chronic excess. Flag products with very high B6 content.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Cell division, DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Low toxicity. Excess excreted. Very rarely causes issues in dogs.
Notes for App: Safe. Critical for pregnant dogs. Natural form (folate) in leafy greens is preferable but synthetic is fine.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Nerve health, red blood cell production, DNA synthesis
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Extremely low toxicity. Excess excreted. Cyanocobalamin contains trace cyanide but negligible amounts.
Notes for App: Methylcobalamin is the preferred bioavailable form. Flag cyanocobalamin — technically safe but inferior quality signal.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Antioxidant, immune support, collagen synthesis
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Dogs synthesize their own Vitamin C. Excess from supplements can cause oxalate kidney stones in predisposed dogs.
Notes for App: Not essential for healthy dogs. Flag if heavily supplemented — may indicate kidney risk in prone breeds.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Calcium & phosphorus absorption, bone health
Long-Term Risk (Excess): TOXICITY RISK: Hypercalcemia — calcium deposits in kidneys, heart, blood vessels. Kidney failure and death possible. Dogs cannot tolerate excess Vitamin D like humans.
Notes for App: 🚨 FLAG THIS. One of the most dangerous vitamins for dogs in excess. Several pet food recalls involved Vitamin D3 overdose. If a product has D3 added AND fish meal, double-flag.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Antioxidant, immune function, skin and coat health
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Synthetic dl-alpha tocopherol is less bioavailable. Very high doses may interfere with Vitamin K absorption.
Organs / Systems Affected: Immune system, skin, muscles, reproductive system
Notes for App: Natural d-alpha tocopherol (no 'l') is better. Synthetic dl-alpha is okay but lower quality. Flag synthetic form as 'acceptable but not ideal'.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Blood clotting, bone metabolism
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Menadione (K3 synthetic): linked to liver toxicity, hemolytic anemia, and immune system damage in long-term use. K1 (phylloquinone) is safe.
Safe Daily Range (Dog): Not established — usually sufficient from food
Notes for App: 🚨 FLAG MENADIONE (K3). It is banned in human supplements in the US but still used in some pet foods. Always flag this ingredient. K1 is fine.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Fatty acid synthesis, metabolism, healthy coat and paws
Long-Term Risk (Excess): No known toxicity in dogs. Excess excreted safely.
Notes for App: Raw egg whites block biotin absorption — relevant if owner feeds raw eggs.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Brain function, liver health, fat transport
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Excess: fishy body odor, GI issues, low blood pressure. Liver can be stressed at very high doses.
Notes for App: Essential nutrient. Synthetic choline chloride is the standard added form. Generally safe.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Bone and teeth formation, muscle contraction, nerve signaling
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Excess: skeletal deformities in large-breed puppies, soft tissue calcification, kidney stones. Deficiency causes rickets.
Notes for App: ⚠️ Large-breed puppies especially sensitive. Flag high calcium in puppy formulas. Balance with phosphorus ratio (1.2:1 Ca:P ideal).

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Bone structure, energy metabolism (ATP), cell membrane health
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Excess phosphorus damages kidneys over time. Dogs with CKD (chronic kidney disease) must have restricted phosphorus.
Notes for App: 🚨 Flag for dogs with kidney issues. High phosphorus in foods accelerates kidney disease progression.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Muscle and nerve function, protein synthesis, energy production
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Excess: diarrhea, low blood pressure, muscle weakness. Magnesium oxide poorly absorbed — can cause GI upset.
Notes for App: Magnesium oxide is cheap and poorly bioavailable. Magnesium citrate or glycinate are better forms. Note form in your app.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Heart rhythm, fluid balance, muscle contraction
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Excess rare from food. Deficiency (hypokalemia) causes muscle weakness, heart arrhythmia.
Notes for App: Safe at normal dietary levels. Flag absence — especially in weight loss or restricted diets.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Fluid balance, nerve transmission, blood pressure regulation
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Excess: hypertension, kidney strain, heart disease worsening. Dogs with heart/kidney disease need low sodium.
Notes for App: ⚠️ Flag high sodium for dogs with heart or kidney disease. Many pet foods have excess sodium as flavor enhancer.

Synthetic Form Added: Zinc Sulfate / Zinc Oxide / Zinc Proteinate
Short-Term Effect on Dog: Immune function, wound healing, skin and coat health, enzyme function
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Zinc oxide: poor bioavailability. Zinc toxicity: hemolytic anemia, liver and kidney damage. Some breeds (Huskies, Malamutes) have zinc malabsorption.
Notes for App: Zinc proteinate/chelate is the best bioavailable form. Zinc oxide is cheap and poorly absorbed. Flag oxide form as lower quality.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Oxygen transport (hemoglobin), energy metabolism
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Iron overload: liver damage, oxidative stress. Ferric oxide is essentially unabsorbable and used as a colorant.
Notes for App: 🚨 Ferric oxide is a cosmetic colorant with no nutritional value — flag it. Ferrous sulfate is the acceptable supplemental form.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Iron metabolism, collagen formation, nervous system health
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Copper storage disease: Bedlington Terriers, Labrador Retrievers, Dalmatians genetically predisposed to copper accumulation in liver. Cirrhosis and liver failure.
Notes for App: 🚨 BREED FLAG. Copper toxicosis is a serious concern. Flag high copper for predisposed breeds. Copper proteinate is safer than copper sulfate.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Bone development, enzyme activation, antioxidant defense
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Low toxicity from food sources. Very high doses: neurological effects (rare from diet).
Notes for App: Generally safe. Proteinate form better absorbed than sulfate.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Antioxidant (glutathione peroxidase), thyroid hormone metabolism, immune function
Long-Term Risk (Excess): NARROW margin between deficiency and toxicity. Excess (selenosis): vomiting, diarrhea, hair loss, neurological damage, death at high doses.
Notes for App: 🚨 Very narrow safe range. Selenium yeast is more bioavailable and safer than sodium selenite. Flag sodium selenite as lower quality form.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Thyroid hormone production, metabolic rate regulation
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Excess iodine can CAUSE hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism paradoxically. Some dogs sensitive to iodine spikes from seaweed/kelp additives.
Notes for App: ⚠️ Flag products with both potassium iodide AND kelp/seaweed — double iodine source. Thyroid disruption risk.

Short-Term Effect on Dog: Heart muscle function, eye health, bile acid conjugation, antioxidant
Long-Term Risk (Excess): Taurine deficiency linked to DCM (dilated cardiomyopathy) — especially in grain-free diets with legumes. No known toxicity from excess.
Notes for App: 🚨 FLAG absence in grain-free formulas. FDA investigated DCM link to grain-free diets. Taurine should be added if peas/lentils/chickpeas are main ingredients.
